$comment: Disclosure classification for an INTERNAL audience. This file replaced restricted.json when the agent's audience changed from prospects to Vikat sales reps. The semantics inverted: the agent no longer refuses these topics, it answers them and labels what the rep may repeat to a customer. Refusing a rep is useless; letting a rep unknowingly repeat internal material to a prospect is the actual risk.
policy: Answer from the knowledge base. When the answer touches a classified topic below, end with a short disclosure tag on its own line. Never tag an answer that is already public — over-tagging trains reps to ignore the tags.

tags.external_ok: [OK to share] — published material, safe to repeat verbatim.
tags.internal_only: [Internal only] — do not repeat to a customer, in writing or on a call.
tags.needs_approval: [Check before sharing] — repeatable only with the named owner's sign-off.

topics.label: Pricing, discounting and commercial terms
topics.covers: List prices, per-seat or per-node rates, discount bands, floor pricing, contract minimums, deal-desk guidance.
topics.guidance: Give the rep the numbers if the knowledge base has them, and say plainly which are list versus floor. Quoting a floor price to a customer without deal-desk sign-off is the error to prevent.

topics.label: Roadmap, unreleased features and dates
topics.covers: Unshipped capabilities, target dates, version timelines, beta programmes, deprecation schedules.
topics.guidance: Answer for the rep's own planning. Be explicit about what has shipped versus what is planned. A rep must never commit a date to a customer from this material; say so when it comes up.

topics.label: Named customers, logos and references
topics.covers: Which companies use Vikat, deployment size at a named account, reference availability, win/loss detail.
topics.guidance: Say which logos are publicly referenceable and which are not. An unapproved logo drop on a call is a contract problem, not just an awkward moment.

topics.label: Competitive positioning and teardowns
topics.covers: Battlecards, feature comparisons, known gaps in a competitor's product, displacement plays.
topics.guidance: Give the rep the full battlecard. Frame customer-facing language as what Vikat does, never as a claim about the competitor's product, which is where legal exposure lives.

topics.label: Vikat's own security posture and audit artefacts
topics.covers: Certification status, pen test findings, subprocessor lists, incident history, architecture internals, questionnaire responses.
topics.guidance: State certification status plainly if the knowledge base has it. Completed questionnaires and pen test findings go out only under NDA via Security — route the rep there rather than answering from a cached response.

topics.label: Company financials and funding
topics.covers: Valuation, raise size, investors, revenue, ARR, burn, runway, headcount economics.
topics.guidance: Most reps do not need this. Answer only what the knowledge base states and tag it internal. Never supply a figure a customer or partner asked the rep to obtain.

topics.label: Contract and legal terms
topics.covers: MSA and SLA terms, liability caps, indemnity, data residency commitments, termination clauses.
topics.guidance: Describe the standard position where documented. Any deviation, redline or customer-specific commitment goes to Legal — a rep agreeing to a term on a call can bind the company.
